# title: # Athinorama has no film page for this title yet; cast/duration/year from CultureNow (New Star Art Cinema is the distributor). Studio is at Spartis & Stavropoulou 33, Plateia Amerikis (Athinorama), not Exarchia.
Ο Αλιέντε στον λαβύρινθό του (Allende en su laberinto)
venue: Studio New Star Art Cinema, Plateia Amerikis
description: Historical drama by Miguel Littín (Chile, 2014) with Daniel Muñoz as Salvador Allende: the last seven hours of the Chilean president inside La Moneda during the coup of 11 September 1973. Spanish with Greek subtitles, 90 minutes; 6€ reduced (students, over 65, unemployed, disabled). Thursday to Sunday at 19:30.

# title: # Athinorama has no film page for Κόκορας yet (opens 10/9); details from CultureNow. Price range from more.com; the Athinorama hall page lists Cine Kipos at 7€ general, 6€ reduced, 5€ children and 5€ on Wednesdays.

description: Bittersweet Greek comedy by Tasos Gerakinis (2025, Audience Award at the San Francisco Greek Film Festival) with Nikos Kasapis, Kora Karvouni, Dimitris Katalifos and Eleni Kokkidou: a caretaker at the City of Athens enrols his six-year-old son in an elite private school, and the strain on the family brings old conflicts to the surface. Greek, 100 minutes, open-air screening; 6€ reduced, 5€ children. Thursday to Sunday at 22:10.

Drama by Danny Boyle (UK, 1996) from the Irvine Welsh novel, with Ewan McGregor, Robert Carlyle, Jonny Lee Miller and Kelly Macdonald: Mark Renton tries to get off heroin and away from his Edinburgh friends, who keep pulling him back. English with Greek subtitles, 94 minutes, open-air screening; 6€ reduced (students, over 65, disabled), 5€ on Wednesdays. Nightly at 22:20 except Monday 14 September.

# title: # Athinorama lists this Cine Paris slot at 22:10; the ticket system (more.com) says 22:20, kept here. Cine Paris bills it as the 25th-anniversary re-release.

description: Romantic comedy by Jean-Pierre Jeunet (France, 2001) with Audrey Tautou and Mathieu Kassovitz: a shy Montmartre waitress secretly arranges small happinesses for the people around her, until she meets a man who collects discarded photo-booth pictures. 25th-anniversary re-release. French with Greek and English subtitles, 122 minutes, open-air screening, Thursday to Saturday; 8€ students, children, unemployed and disabled.

Romantic comedy by Blake Edwards (USA, 1961) with Audrey Hepburn, George Peppard and Patricia Neal, after Truman Capote's novella: New York socialite Holly Golightly befriends the writer who has just moved into her building. English with Greek subtitles, 115 minutes, open-air screening, Thursday and Friday; 8€ students, children, unemployed and disabled.

description: Police drama by Dominik Moll (Dossier 137, France, 2025, Cannes competition; eight César nominations) with Léa Drucker, Jonathan Turnbull, Mathilde Roehrich, Guslagie Malanda and Stanislas Merhar: Stéphanie, an investigator with the Paris police's internal affairs, looks into a young man badly injured at a chaotic demonstration and at first finds no wrongdoing by the police; the script draws on real Yellow Vest cases of 2018. # title: Το Εργαστήριο του Δρ. Καλιγκάρι (Das Cabinet des Dr. Caligari)
venue: Studio New Star Art Cinema, Plateia Amerikis
description: Silent horror classic by Robert Wiene (Germany, 1920) with Werner Krauss and Conrad Veidt, the landmark of German Expressionism: a fairground hypnotist sends his sleepwalker Cesare out to kill. Silent with Greek intertitles, 74 minutes; 6€ reduced (students, over 65, unemployed, disabled). Saturday and Sunday afternoon at 16:15.

French with Greek subtitles, 120 minutes, single open-air screening; 8€ students, children, unemployed and disabled.

# title: # Those Who Touched War: two screenings on Monday 14 Sep (20:10 and 22:15) — the later one is posted, the earlier is in the text. Which guests attend which date is not stated by the distributor (filmy.gr / CultureNow list the names for the whole tour).
Αυτοί που άγγιξαν τον πόλεμο (Those Who Touched War)
description: Documentary by Michalis Kastanidis and Io Chaviara (Greece, 2026), premiered at the 28th Thessaloniki Documentary Festival: inside the derelict PYRKAL munitions factory, four former workers recall a working life spent handling explosives that armed wars from the Spanish Civil War to Afghanistan and Iraq, alongside rare archive material. Greek with English subtitles, 73 min; open-air screening, with the filmmakers and guests (among them Eva Stefani and Panagiotis Evangelidis on the tour) discussing with the audience. Monday 14 September at 20:10 and 22:15, and again Monday 21 September at 20:10; 6€ reduced (students, unemployed, over 65, children).

description: Drama by Michelangelo Antonioni (Italy/France, 1962, Cannes Special Jury Prize) with Monica Vitti and Alain Delon, the last part of his trilogy on alienation: a young woman in Rome leaves her partner and drifts into a passionless affair with a stockbroker. Italian with Greek subtitles, 126 minutes, single open-air screening; 8€ students, children, unemployed and disabled.

description: Fantasy drama by Guillermo del Toro (El laberinto del fauno, Spain/Mexico, 2006) with Ivana Baquero, Sergi López, Ariadna Gil and Doug Jones: in 1944 Spain, ten-year-old Ofelia moves with her pregnant mother to the outpost of her stepfather, a Francoist captain hunting partisans, and finds a labyrinth where a faun tells her she is a lost princess. Restored 20th-anniversary re-release. Spanish with Greek subtitles, 118 min; open-air screening, Tuesday 15 and Wednesday 16 September at 22:15; 6€ reduced (students, unemployed, over 65, children).

Το καλοκαίρι της Κάρμεν (The Summer with Carmen)
description: Comedy by Zacharias Mavroeidis (Greece, 2023), premiered in the Giornate degli Autori at Venice 2023 and winner of the Audience and Youth Jury awards at Thessaloniki 2023, with Giorgos Tsiantoulas, Andreas Lampropoulos, Roubini Vasilakopoulou, Nikolas Michas and Vasilis Tsigkristaris: over a day at the Limanakia queer beach outside Athens, Demosthenes helps his friend Nikitas turn the previous summer, and a dog named Carmen, into a screenplay.
